newsitem.title: USA: Dlr ends lower in US, uncertainty over Fed lingers.
newsitem.headline: Dlr ends lower in US, uncertainty over Fed lingers.

text.p: *Dlr ends lower in US against mark and yen, market opinion divided over outcome of FOMC meeting on March 25. *Dlr still holds some gains earned overseas in run-up to release of Feb 0.3 pct CPI gain. Core CPI +0.2 pct. *Dlr/yen earlier topped 123 but slid as dealers await US trade data 0830 EST Thurs. Mark/yen weakness also weighs on dollar/yen
The dollar ended modestly lower on Wednesday after uncertainty over the future of U.S. interest rates put a dent in solid overnight gains.
Financial markets had been anxiously awaiting the U.S. consumer price index (CPI), the last batch of crucial inflation data before next week's Federal Reserve policy meeting on interest rates.
But the report yielded few clues. Consumer prices rose by 0.3 percent in February, only a whisper higher than the 0.2 percent expected by economists.
The closely scrutinized core rate, which excludes the volatile food and energy sectors, rose 0.2 percent, as expected.
Analysts said the report painted a picture of relatively subdued price gains, but refused to rule out a preemptive strike against inflation from the Fed.

"It's not a troublesome surge in inflation," said Joseph Liro, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Corp. "But I don't think the Fed really needs anything much more than what they're seeing right now to raise rates."
The dollar ended the day at 1.6800/05 marks, down from 1.6825/35 marks at the open. Against the yen, the dollar retreated to 122.79/84 from 123.04/09 in early trade.

The dollar opened U.S. trade higher, helped by overnight weakness in the German mark, which came under pressure after several days of gains. The mark was heavily bought on Monday and Tuesday at the expense of the British pound after British Prime Minister John Major's call for an election on May 1.
But investors moved back into sterling after surprisingly strong employment and retail sales figures in the U.K. highlighted the health of Britain's economy.
"That helped continue to push the mark lower pretty much across the board," said Ben Strauss, assistant vice president at Bank Julius Baer and Co.
But dollar/mark weakened as the U.S. session unfolded and dollar/yen followed suit as dealers grew cautious ahead of U.S. trade data, due Thursday.

Many analysts expect the report to show a widening in the U.S. bilateral trade deficit with Japan. This could spur trade tensions between the two countries and result in calls from U.S. exporters for a weaker dollar to boost U.S. competitiveness.

"The trade data coming tomorrow is important," said Bob Lynch, senior currency analyst at MMS International. "Dollar/yen has had a nice rebound but with heightened sensitivity from U.S. officials on the trade data, that may have encouraged some profit-taking."

In other trade on Wednesday, sterling closed at $1.5979/84, up from $1.5964/69 at the open. The dollar ended weaker at 1.4420/30 Swiss francs, down from its opening rate of 1.4460/70. The dollar settled at Canadian $1.3771/76 versus C$1.3762/67, while the Australian dollar ended at $0.7870/75 against $0.7865/70.
